vframegen.config.title: VFrameGen
vframegen.sodium.allSettings.tooltip: Opens the full settings screen: limits, reprojection, frame pacing and debug options.
vframegen.firstRun.title: VFrameGen is set up
vframegen.firstRun.message: %s preset, %s fps target, picked for your PC. Change it in Video Settings.
vframegen.config.preset.tooltip:
Sets frame generation, render scale, upscaling and anti-aliasing together. Changing any of them by hand makes it Custom. The target frame rate and motion blur are left as they are.
Low-end: dynamic render scale, bicubic upscaling, FXAA. For PCs that struggle to hold the target.
Balanced: dynamic render scale, SMAA.
Quality: full resolution with temporal anti-aliasing; frame generation only for smoothness.
vframegen.config.enabled.tooltip: Show generated frames between real frames.
vframegen.config.multiplier.tooltip:
Frames shown per real frame. 2x shows one generated frame per real one, 6x shows five.
Each extra frame costs a little GPU time but no extra VRAM.
With VSync on, real frames are capped at your refresh rate divided by this.
vframegen.config.adaptive.tooltip:
Instead of the fixed multiplier, picks how many frames to show per real frame (1 to 8, beyond the fixed multiplier's 6) to reach the target frame rate, as the real frame rate changes.
Real frames are capped at the target; when they reach it alone, no frames are generated.
The target is not always reached: every generated frame takes some GPU time, so the real frame rate drops a little as more are made, and when the GPU is already maxed out (a heavy shader pack) adaptive mode settles below the target rather than slowing the game down further.
vframegen.config.targetFps.tooltip: Frames per second to show, real and generated together: the target of adaptive frame generation and of dynamic render scale (which aims for half of it in real frames while frame generation is on). Your display's refresh rate is a good choice.
vframegen.config.mode.tooltip:
Interpolated: each real frame is held back by one frame and the frames between are built from both neighbours. No smearing at the screen edges, even pacing, about one real frame more input lag.
Low latency: built from the last real frame only. No added lag, but edges smear when turning and frames can bunch up when the CPU is the bottleneck.
vframegen.config.depthMode.tooltip:
Depth: correct parallax when moving.
Rotation only: ignores depth; exact when turning, approximate when moving. A fallback for shader packs whose depth buffer does not line up.
Auto: Depth.
vframegen.config.pacing.tooltip:
Balanced: hold the generated frame back to the middle of the real-frame interval, when the GPU is the bottleneck anyway.
Off: show it as soon as it is ready.
Only generate frames while no menu or inventory is open.
vframegen.config.maxCameraJumpBlocks.too: No generated frame across a camera jump larger than this, such as a teleport.
vframegen.config.maxCameraTurnDegrees.to: No generated frame when the camera turned more than this between two real frames. 0 = no limit.
vframegen.config.maxRealFrameAgeMs.toolt: Generation pauses when real frames take longer than this. 100 ms = below 10 FPS.
vframegen.config.sharpness.tooltip: Unsharp mask on generated frames. 0 = off.
vframegen.config.antiAliasing.tooltip:
Smooths jagged edges on the world (not the GUI). Works with or without frame generation.
FXAA: the cheapest, softens the image a little.
SMAA: finds edge shapes, so edges come out cleaner and textures stay sharper. Costs a little more GPU time.
Most shader packs have their own anti-aliasing: leave this off with one. Not used with the Temporal upscaler, which anti-aliases on its own.
vframegen.config.antiAliasingQuality.too: Higher catches fainter and longer edges and smooths them more fully, at more GPU time. Low is the cheapest.
vframegen.config.opticalFlow.tooltip: Uses your GPU's optical flow hardware to measure how the picture moved between real frames. Generated frames then also follow what depth alone can't predict: mob limbs, fire, particles, water and animated textures. Interpolated mode only. Costs about a quarter of a millisecond per frame.
vframegen.packBlur.title: Shader pack motion blur is on
vframegen.packBlur.message: It ghosts with frame generation. Turn it off in the pack's settings and use VFrameGen's Motion blur (Quality).
vframegen.config.motionBlur.tooltip: Camera motion blur on every frame shown, real and generated, along that frame's own motion. Turn your shader pack's motion blur off: it smears whole real frames, which ghosts with frame generation.
vframegen.config.motionBlurStrength.tool: Blur length, as a share of the time between shown frames (50% is like a 180° film shutter).
vframegen.config.guiDiffThreshold.toolti: How much the GUI pass must change a pixel for it to be kept still instead of reprojected.
vframegen.config.debugTint.tooltip: Tints generated frames magenta, to see which frames are generated.
vframegen.config.renderScale.tooltip:
Renders the world (and the shader pack) at this fraction of the window size, then upscales it. The GUI stays sharp. 100% = off. 75% shades about 56% of the pixels.
Not used while dynamic render scale is on.
vframegen.config.dynamicRenderScale.tool:
Lowers the render scale when real frames are too slow for the target frame rate (General), and raises it again when there is room. With frame generation on it aims for half the target in real frames (or the target / multiplier); frame generation makes up the rest. Between 50% and 100%; the render scale setting is not used while this is on.
For busy scenes on a weaker PC: the frame rate stays steadier, and the image is only softer while it has to be.
vframegen.config.upscaler.tooltip:
Bicubic: Catmull-Rom with contrast-adaptive sharpening, the fastest.
Edge-adaptive: FSR 1 style (EASU + RCAS). Follows edges, so they stay sharp without jaggies or halos. Costs a little more GPU time.
Temporal: builds full-resolution detail from several frames, each shifted by a fraction of a pixel. The sharpest at low render scale, and anti-aliases too (FXAA/SMAA are skipped), even at 100%. Moving mobs can leave faint trails. Uses edge-adaptive while a shader pack is on.
vframegen.config.upscaleSharpness.toolti: Sharpening after the upscale. With Bicubic, 0% = plain bicubic. With Edge-adaptive, this is the RCAS strength (0% = off).
vframegen.config.displayHz.tooltip: The refresh rate the auto frame cap divides by the multiplier. Starts at your monitor's refresh rate, rounded up (179.96 Hz reads 180), and follows it while left there. Set it by hand if that is wrong (some streaming virtual displays report 60 Hz while running at 120).
vframegen.config.presentThread.tooltip: Shows each frame at its exact time from a separate thread, like FSR 3 and DLSS frame generation. Generated frames stay evenly spaced without a frame cap. Needs a restart.
vframegen.config.debugCaptures.tooltip: F8 (or the controller capture button) saves the next frames as images into vframegen-debug in the game folder.
vframegen.config.debugOpticalFlow.toolti: Measures optical flow on every real frame even when it isn't used, and F8 saves it as an image.
vframegen.config.debugFrameLog.tooltip: Keeps a record of the last ~10 seconds of frames sent to the screen (real or generated, time, camera position). F8 saves it. Costs a little memory churn.
vframegen.config.debugStatsLog.tooltip: Every 5 seconds, writes frame rates, timings and why frames were skipped to the game log.
vframegen.config.debugPacingLog.tooltip: Every second, writes how evenly frames reached the screen to the game log.
vframegen.config.debugStallLog.tooltip: Writes a breakdown of every game loop that took over 35 ms to the game log (which part of the frame took long, and garbage collection).
vframegen.capture.off: VFrameGen: debug captures are off (Mod Menu → VFrameGen → Debug)
vframegen.config.autoCap.tooltip: When Max Framerate is unlimited, caps real frames at your display's refresh rate divided by the multiplier while frame generation runs. Generated frames are shown in the idle time this leaves, so they stay evenly spaced.
vframegen.controller.capture.description: Save the next burst of real and generated frames to vframegen-debug (same as F8).
vframegen.controller.toggle.description: Turn frame generation on or off (same as F9).
vframegen.vsync.title: Keep VSync on with frame generation?
vframegen.vsync.message: VSync makes frame generation stutter heavily: generated frames get shown twice or dropped. Frame generation already paces frames by itself, so VSync is normally best left off.
